summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of Addison’s disease and Hashimoto’s thyroiditis was admitted after experiencing syncope at home, with subsequent head impact, vomiting, and fecal incontinence. Evaluation revealed dehydration and acute kidney injury with elevated creatinine, but no intracranial hemorrhage on head CT, no cardiac arrhythmias on telemetry, and no urinary infection. She was treated with intravenous fluids and remained on her home dose of prednisone 5mg daily, with no signs of adrenal insufficiency. Her symptoms resolved, and she was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to maintain hydration, continue her medications, and follow up as needed.
